items.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023
items.q: And you know my cousin Sherry — she had a new boyfriend, she wanted a new poem written about them so I’d just do that and then charge them a little bit of money for it.

ctx.x: Do you read through your lyrics when they’re in progress as if they’re a poem?

Yeah. I do. I do. Melodically, melody is important to me. Groove is even, right up there with melody, but it’s about the words, the lyrics and I started out writing poetry as a © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

young person. Some of my favorite poets were Dr. Maya Angelou and Gwendolyn Brooks, Nikki Giovanni, which I actually got a chance to talk to and see. These were some of my favorites, you know black poetresses. That was huge for me, growing up in the small town, being this little black girl in the middle of Texas. I wanted to read something that I could relate to, something that was written that said, basically told me — gave me an idea that someone else out there like me, and Maya Angelou was huge in my life…
